text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Turkish Ambassador to Bosnia Mehmet Gorkay and military attache Cemil Yurdakul tell Moslem-Croat Federation Defence Minister Ante Jelavic that Turkey will continue support to federal army training in Turkey within the U.S.-backed "train-and-equip" programme.
- Federation Defence Minister Ante Jelavic meets Egyptian Ambassador Ahmed Abdul Rahman Abu Taleb who expresses hope for future cooperation with federal army and the defence ministry.
- Two unidentified assailants from Croat-controlled part of divided town of Mostar fired two rifle grenades at Moslem-held sector on Monday but no casualties reported.
- World Bank gives 500,000 German marks for agricultural development in Posavina region, Bosnian Croat news agency Habena quotes local Bank official Joso Vincetic as saying.
- Bosnian collective presidency meets in Serb-held Sarajevo suburb of Lukavica and predicts agreement for reconstruction of country to be signed on February 7.
- Moslem-Croat Federation Forum, which met on Monday to try to overcome disputes between partners, will in future meet once a week, diplomatic source tells paper.
- Implementation of central bank for Bosnia has been stalled by demands from Bosnian Serb entity to maintain separate currency, spokesman for international High Representative for Bosnia says.
